captions.instagram:
How do you build your shoulders?

The shoulder is a golf ball on a tee: the most mobile joint you have, held on mostly by muscle. Raise an arm and watch the blade turn with it, work out why a 5 kg dumbbell feels heavy out to the side, swing a gada, and learn to train it safely.

→ Your shoulder is a big ball on a small, shallow socket, like a golf ball on a tee.
→ A three-part deltoid caps it, and four rotator cuff muscles hold the ball in place.
→ Raise your arm and the shoulder blade turns too: about 1° for every 2° at the ball.
→ The rotator cuff pulls the ball into its socket so the deltoid can lift instead of slide.
→ A 5 kg dumbbell held out to the side twists your shoulder with about 40 N·m.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/shouldersclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How do you build your shoulders? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
The shoulder is a golf ball on a tee: the most mobile joint you have, held on mostly by muscle. Raise an arm and watch the blade turn with it, work out why a 5 kg dumbbell feels heavy out to the side, swing a gada, and learn to train it safely.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/shouldersclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/shouldersclear

In this video:
• A golf ball on a tee. Three bones meet at the shoulder: the collarbone, the shoulder blade and the humerus.
• The ball and the blade share every raise. Lift your arm 180° and roughly 120° happens at the ball and 60° comes from the shoulder blade turning on your ribs: the 2:1 scapulohumeral rhythm measured in 1944.
• Leverage makes light weights heavy. In a lateral raise a 5 kg dumbbell 63 cm out twists the shoulder with about 31 N·m, plus 10 N·m from your own arm, peaking at 90°.
• Hard sets, patience and balance. Muscle grows from tension and sets taken close to failure, about 10 or more a week per muscle, with light or heavy loads.
• Train without pain. Most shoulder pain settles with exercise; surgery to shave the acromion did no better than placebo in the 2018 CSAW trial.
• From akhara to clinic. Indian wrestlers swung the gada and jodi for centuries, and British soldiers took the clubs home in the 1800s as Indian clubs.
